questions.q: Which of the following processes of physical weathering is most characteristic of the hot, semi-arid regions of West Africa, causing the outer layers of a rock to repeatedly expand and contract until they peel off?
questions.explain: **Exfoliation** (often called "onion-skin" weathering) occurs in environments with a high diurnal (daily) temperature range. Intense daytime heating causes the rock's outer layers to expand, while rapid nighttime cooling causes them to contract. Over time, this stress causes the outer layers to peel away. Carbonation and hydration are *chemical* weathering processes, while frost shattering requires freezing temperatures.

questions.q: An ox-bow lake is a distinct geographical landform created by the denudational action of running water. In which section of a river's profile is this feature predominantly found?
options: The steep-sided upper course near the river's source
The area immediately below a large waterfall
The deep, V-shaped valleys of the middle course
The broad, meandering floodplains of the lower course
questions.explain: An **ox-bow lake** forms in the gently sloping **lower course** (the senile or old-age stage) of a river. At this stage, lateral erosion and deposition cause the river to meander extensively. Eventually, a meander loop may be cut off during a flood, leaving behind a crescent-shaped body of water on the floodplain.

questions.q: In arid environments like the fringes of the Sahara Desert, the wind carries coarse sand particles that heavily erode the softer lower portions of a standing rock outcrop faster than the harder upper parts. This differential abrasion results in the formation of a:
questions.explain: A **rock pedestal** (or mushroom rock) is created by wind abrasion. Wind naturally carries its heaviest and most abrasive sand particles close to the ground (usually within $1$ to $2$ meters of the surface). This undercuts the base of the rock, leaving a wide, un-eroded top resting on a narrow base.

questions.q: Along the West African coastline, sediments such as sand and shingle are continuously transported along the beach in a zig-zag pattern. This occurs when waves strike the shore at an oblique angle and the backwash pulls material straight down under gravity. This transport process is known as:
questions.explain: **Longshore drift** is the lateral movement of material along a coastline. It is driven by the prevailing wind, which causes the swash to push material up the beach at an angle, while gravity pulls the backwash directly down. Over time, this moves material horizontally, often leading to the formation of depositional features like spits and bars.
